Compute the efficiency ratio by multiplying the true wind speed by the boat speed, and dividing by the mainsail sheet tension. Return this efficiency ratio. If the string format is bad or a number is unreadable, the adjustment must fail. Example input: 45:15.5:8.0:90:120.0:80.5:40.0:5 yields 1.0333333.

title: Tokamak Plasma Confinement Tuner
spec: Adjust a fusion reactor's parameters using a comma delimited configuration string. The function `tune(plasma)` must read eight distinct values: magnetic field strength, plasma current, electron density, ion temperature, confinement time, major radius, minor radius, and input power. Parse the plasma current and electron density as integers, and the other six values as floating point numbers. Calculate the fusion triple product by multiplying the electron density, ion temperature, and confinement time together. Return this final product. Reject the configuration entirely if any value is missing or invalid. Example input: 5.5,15000000,10,150.0,2.5,6.2,2.0,50.0 yields 3750.0.

title: Fiber Optic Signal Attenuator
spec: Evaluate network cable degradation via a pipe separated string of physical properties. The function `attenuate(splice)` extracts eight measurements: core diameter mismatch, numerical aperture, refractive index, lateral offset, angular misalignment, gap distance, light wavelength, and base splice loss. Parse the wavelength and lateral offset as integers, and the other six as decimal numbers. Determine the signal quality by dividing the numerical aperture by the core diameter mismatch, and subtracting the angular misalignment. Return this signal quality value. If any measurement fails to parse, return an error. Example input: 0.5|0.25|1.45|2|1.5|0.1|1550|0.02 yields -1.0.

title: Bionic Appendage Synchronizer
spec: Synchronize a prosthetic arm using a space separated string of real time telemetry. The function `synchronize(telemetry)` reads eight fields: elbow torque, wrist rotation angle, finger grip force, tactile feedback intensity, motor temperature, battery voltage, nerve impulse rate, and communication latency. Parse the wrist rotation, impulse rate, and latency as integers, and the remaining five fields as floats. Compute the responsiveness score by multiplying the nerve impulse rate by the finger grip force, and dividing by the latency. Return this score. The synchronization aborts if any telemetry field is invalid. Example input: 15.5 90 25.0 5.5 38.0 24.5 120 15 yields 200.0.

title: Powered Exoskeleton Balancer
spec: Maintain upright posture using a dash delimited string of suit sensor values. The function `assist(posture)` extracts eight metrics: hip joint angle, knee flex angle, ankle torque, payload mass, center of gravity x axis, center of gravity y axis, gyroscope pitch, and gyroscope roll. Parse the hip angle, knee flex, and gyroscope pitch as integers, and the other five metrics as floating point numbers. Calculate the stability compensation by adding the hip angle and knee flex, multiplying by the payload mass, and dividing by the ankle torque. Return this compensation value. If the sensor string cannot be fully parsed, the process must fail and return nothing. Example input: 15-30-45.0-80.0-0.5-0.2-5-2.5 yields 80.0.

title: Ancient Pottery Kiln Logs
spec: Write a function `pottery(log)` that processes ancient pottery firing data. The input is a single text string containing multiple lines. Each line contains seven values separated by a pipe symbol: firing phase, clay type, target temperature, hold duration in minutes, airflow rate, humidity percentage, and cooling hours. The function must extract the fields and parse the temperature, duration, airflow, humidity, and cooling hours as whole numbers. If any line is incomplete or contains invalid numbers, the function must immediately return nothing. Otherwise, return an optional whole number representing the sum of the hold durations for all lines where the clay type is the word terracotta. Example input: phase|terracotta|800|40|5|20|12. Output: 40.

title: Apple Orchard Harvest
spec: Write a function `orchard(harvest)` that processes apple picking records. The input is a string of lines, where each line represents a harvested tree. Each line has seven values separated by a comma: tree identifier, apple variety, apples picked, average apple weight in grams, insect bite count, picking hour, and picking minute. The function must extract these segments and parse the last five values as integers. If any line is malformed or any number fails to parse, the function must completely fail and return nothing. If successful, return an optional integer containing the total number of apples picked from trees of the fuji variety. Example input: A1,fuji,50,100,2,10,30. Output: 50.

title: Glacier Ice Core Samples
spec: Write a function `glacier(samples)` that evaluates ice core drilling logs. The input is a text string containing multiple lines. Each line consists of seven fields separated by a semicolon: location name, ice color, drilling depth, carbon dioxide level, methane level, dust concentration, and estimated age in years. Extract these pieces and parse the depth, carbon dioxide, methane, dust, and age as integers. The function must abort and return nothing if any line is missing fields or has unparseable integers. For a successful parse of all lines, return an optional integer that sums the carbon dioxide levels for all lines where the ice color is clear. Example input: site A;clear;150;280;800;15;10000. Output: 280.

title: Knitting Machine Instructions
spec: Write a function `knitting(pattern)` that decodes a sequence of knitting steps. The input is a string with one step per line. Each line contains seven items separated by a colon: row identifier, stitch style, needle size, yarn color, tension level, repeat count, and rest time. Retrieve each item and parse the needle size, tension, repeat count, and rest time as integers. If a line is improperly formatted or a number is invalid, the function must halt and return nothing. On full success, return an optional integer summing the repeat counts for all steps where the stitch style is the word purl. Example input: row five:purl:4:blue:3:10:5. Output: 10.

title: Falcon Hunting Flights
spec: Write a function `falconry(flights)` that aggregates bird flight statistics. The text input contains multiple lines, each representing a single flight with seven fields separated by a dash: bird name, prey type, wind speed, flight altitude, dive speed, flight duration in minutes, and resting time. Isolate each field and parse the wind speed, altitude, dive speed, duration, and resting time as whole numbers. Should any line lack the required fields or contain invalid numbers, the function must return nothing. When all lines are valid, return an optional integer representing the total flight duration for flights where the prey type is the word hare. Example input: apollo-hare-15-200-80-12-30. Output: 12.

title: Cheese Cave Aging Monitor
spec: Write a function `cheese(wheels)` that checks the aging progress of cheese batches. The input text has one line per batch. Each line contains seven values separated by a comma: batch identifier, milk origin, cave humidity percentage, cave temperature, aging days, mold coverage percentage, and turning frequency. Extract all parts and parse the humidity, temperature, aging days, mold coverage, and turning frequency as integers. The function must return nothing immediately if any line is incomplete or contains non-numeric values. Otherwise, return an optional integer representing the sum of aging days for all batches where the milk origin is goat. Example input: batch seven,goat,85,55,120,40,7. Output: 120.

title: Sword Forging Strikes
spec: Write a function `blacksmith(forging)` that reviews hammer strike logs for sword making. The input is a multi-line string. Every line has seven items delimited by a pipe character: weapon identifier, metal type, heating minutes, strike force, anvil angle, fold count, and cooling liquid volume. Separate the items and parse the heating minutes, strike force, anvil angle, fold count, and liquid volume as integers. The function must fail and return nothing if a line is malformed or an integer parse fails. If completely successful, return an optional integer summing the strike force for all lines where the metal type is steel. Example input: sword one|steel|15|200|45|10|5. Output: 200.

title: Juggling Performance Sequence
spec: Write a function `juggling(routine)` that calculates statistics from a juggling act. The input string contains several lines, each detailing a single trick. A line consists of seven fields separated by a semicolon: trick name, prop type, throw height in inches, spin count, hand transfer speed, catch delay, and drop penalty points. Split the line and parse the height, spins, transfer speed, catch delay, and drop penalty as integers. Any missing field or invalid number must cause the function to return nothing. If all lines parse successfully, return an optional integer total of the spin counts for all tricks using the ball prop type. Example input: cascade;ball;30;2;15;5;0. Output: 2.

title: Fragrance Mixing Formula
spec: Write a function `perfume(blend)` that analyzes a custom fragrance recipe. The input string holds one mixing step per line. Each line has seven elements separated by a colon: step name, essential oil, top note drops, middle note drops, base note drops, alcohol volume, and resting days. Read each element and parse the three drop counts, the alcohol volume, and the resting days as integers. If any line is invalid or parsing fails, return nothing. When all lines are valid, return an optional integer totaling the base note drops across all steps where the essential oil is rose. Example input: step one:rose:10:5:8:50:14. Output: 8.

title: Loom Weaving Sequence
spec: Write a function `tapestry(weaving)` that parses instructions for a mechanical loom. The input is a string containing multiple lines. Every line contains seven values separated by a dash: row identifier, thread color, shuttle speed, pattern index, row length, tension setting, and error margin. Extract the fields and parse the speed, pattern index, length, tension, and error margin as whole numbers. The function must immediately return nothing if a line does not conform or parsing fails. For a completely valid input, return an optional integer that adds up the row lengths for all rows where the thread color is gold. Example input: row ten-gold-120-4-50-6-2. Output: 50.

title: Brush Stroke Path Data
spec: Write a function `calligraphy(strokes)` that processes digital brush movements. The input text contains one stroke per line. Each line is made of seven fields separated by a comma: stroke identifier, ink color, brush size, start horizontal coordinate, start vertical coordinate, curve radius, and pressure level. Separate each field and parse the size, both coordinates, radius, and pressure as integers. If any field is missing or cannot be parsed as a number, the function must return nothing. On complete success, return an optional integer summing the pressure levels for all strokes where the ink color is black. Example input: stroke five,black,10,150,200,45,80. Output: 80.

title: Bonsai Tree Shaping Schedule
spec: Write a function `bonsai(pruning)` that aggregates tree care operations. The text input has multiple lines, each with seven items delimited by a pipe character: branch identifier, cut style, wire thickness, bending force, healing days, foliage removed in grams, and rest weeks. Retrieve all items and parse the thickness, force, healing days, foliage, and rest weeks as integers. The function must halt and return nothing if it encounters a bad line or invalid number. If successful, return an optional integer summing the foliage removed for all lines where the cut style is pinch. Example input: branch two|pinch|3|15|30|10|4. Output: 10.

title: Pyrotechnic Show Sequence
spec: Write a function `fireworks(display)` that verifies a firework launch sequence. The multi-line input string contains seven values per line separated by a semicolon: launch tube, visual effect, shell size, burst altitude, fuse delay, blast radius, and sound decibel. Isolate the fields and parse the shell size, altitude, fuse delay, radius, and decibel as integers. The function must fail entirely and return nothing if any line is incomplete or contains non-integers. For valid inputs, return an optional integer totaling the burst altitudes for all lines where the visual effect is peony. Example input: tube four;peony;6;400;3;150;110. Output: 400.

title: Mechanical Watch Assembly
spec: Write a function `clockwork(gears)` that evaluates watch mechanism components. The input string contains one component per line. Each line has seven elements separated by a colon: component name, material, gear teeth count, pinion radius, escapement angle, spring tension, and friction coefficient. Extract the elements and parse the teeth count, pinion radius, angle, tension, and friction as whole numbers. Should any line be improperly formatted or contain invalid digits, the function must return nothing. Otherwise, return an optional integer summing the gear teeth count for all components made of brass. Example input: mainspring:brass:60:12:45:80:5. Output: 60.

title: Fantasy Potion Brewing
spec: Write a function `potions(cauldron)` that analyzes a potion recipe. The input string features one brewing step per line. Each line consists of seven parts separated by a dash: step name, ingredient, stir count, heat level, simmer minutes, magic potency, and cooling time. Isolate each part and parse the stir count, heat level, simmer minutes, potency, and cooling time as integers. The function must immediately return nothing if any line is missing parts or has unparseable numbers. When all lines are correct, return an optional integer totaling the simmer minutes for steps where the ingredient is mint. Example input: step three-mint-10-80-15-50-5. Output: 15.

title: Kite Aerodynamic Testing
spec: Write a function `kite(flying)` that processes kite test flights. The text input contains multiple lines, each representing a flight interval with seven fields separated by a comma: interval identifier, wind direction, wind speed, string length, tension force, pitch angle, and flight altitude. Separate each field and parse the wind speed, string length, tension, pitch, and altitude as integers. The function must return nothing if it finds an incomplete line or a non-numeric value. For a fully valid input, return an optional integer summing the tension force for all intervals where the wind direction is north. Example input: interval one,north,15,100,45,30,80. Output: 45.

title: Marble Carving Tool Paths
spec: Write a function `sculpture(chiseling)` that reviews automated carving instructions. The input string contains multiple lines. Every line contains seven values separated by a pipe symbol: instruction identifier, tool shape, drill depth, approach angle, feed rate, water coolant volume, and surface finish rating. Extract the values and parse the depth, angle, feed rate, coolant volume, and finish rating as integers. If any line is incorrectly formatted or a number fails to parse, return nothing. On complete success, return an optional integer totaling the drill depth for all instructions where the tool shape is flat. Example input: step two|flat|20|45|10|50|8. Output: 20.

title: Fencing Match Actions
spec: Write a function `fencing(bouts)` that calculates statistics from fencing matches. The input text has one action per line. Each line is composed of seven items separated by a semicolon: action identifier, technique, advance steps, lunge speed, parry angle, touch zone, and recovery time. Split the line and parse the advance steps, lunge speed, parry angle, touch zone, and recovery time as integers. The function must abort and return nothing if a line is missing items or contains invalid numbers. If successful, return an optional integer summing the advance steps for all actions where the technique is riposte. Example input: action four;riposte;3;15;45;2;1. Output: 3.

title: Cigar Rolling Instructions
spec: Write a function `cigar(rolling)` that processes tobacco assembly logs. The input string contains multiple lines, each with seven fields separated by a colon: batch identifier, wrapper leaf, filler weight in grams, moisture level, ring gauge, overall length, and pressing time. Retrieve the fields and parse the filler weight, moisture, ring gauge, length, and pressing time as integers. Any missing field or invalid number must cause the function to return nothing. When all lines are valid, return an optional integer representing the total filler weight for batches where the wrapper leaf is maduro. Example input: batch nine:maduro:150:70:52:6:45. Output: 150.

title: Whitewater Canoe Navigation
spec: Write a function `canoe(rapids)` that evaluates river navigation telemetry. The input string contains one reading per line. Each line consists of seven elements separated by a dash: reading identifier, river hazard, water flow rate, rock distance, paddle stroke count, lean angle, and boat speed. Isolate the elements and parse the flow rate, rock distance, stroke count, lean angle, and speed as integers. The function must fail and return nothing if a line is malformed or an integer parse fails. For fully correct inputs, return an optional integer summing the paddle stroke count for readings where the hazard is eddy. Example input: reading six-eddy-200-15-4-30-10. Output: 4.

title: Glassblowing Shaping Steps
spec: Write a function `glassblowing(furnace)` that summarizes glass creation logs. The text input features one step per line with seven values separated by a comma: step identifier, glass color, gather size, pipe rotation speed, blow pressure, glory hole time, and anneal temperature. Separate each value and parse the gather size, rotation speed, pressure, glory hole time, and anneal temperature as integers. Should any line lack fields or contain invalid numbers, the function must return nothing. On success, return an optional integer totaling the glory hole time for all steps where the glass color is blue. Example input: step one,blue,5,30,12,45,900. Output: 45.

title: Harp String Tension Calibration
spec: Write a function `harp(tuning)` that analyzes instrument tuning data. The input is a multi-line string. Every line has seven items delimited by a pipe character: string identifier, musical note, pedal position, tension pounds, frequency hertz, thickness, and age in months. Extract the items and parse the pedal position, tension, frequency, thickness, and age as integers. The function must return nothing immediately if a line is incomplete or contains non-numeric values. Otherwise, return an optional integer representing the sum of the tension pounds for all strings where the musical note is c. Example input: string four|c|1|40|261|2|12. Output: 40.

title: Classic Barbershop Service
spec: Write a function `barber(shaves)` that reviews shaving service records. The input string contains several lines, each detailing a customer session. A line consists of seven fields separated by a semicolon: customer identifier, beard type, towel temperature, blade sharpness, lather volume, stroke angle, and shave duration. Split the line and parse the towel temperature, blade sharpness, lather volume, stroke angle, and duration as integers. Any missing field or invalid number must cause the function to return nothing. If all lines parse successfully, return an optional integer totaling the shave duration for sessions where the beard type is coarse. Example input: customer ten;coarse;110;9;50;35;15. Output: 15.
